bug_info.bug_desc: In StSendData, when an isochronous IN transaction terminates, the FSM unconditionally asserted in_xact_end, signaling successful transaction completion even if the endpoint had no data available. Per the specification, an isochronous endpoint with no data must send a zero-length DATA0 packet and must not indicate a data completion. The old behavior therefore produced a spurious transaction-complete/packet-sent notification for every zero-length isochronous response.
bug_info.fix_hint: Gate the isochronous completion indication on whether the selected endpoint actually supplied data. When the isochronous data packet ends, assert in_xact_end only if in_ep_has_data_i for the current endpoint is set, so zero-length responses with no buffer/data do not report completion while real data payloads still do.
